title: TP stability fixes (runtime 1.19) — canary rollout checklist
content:
Doc purpose
- This is the step-by-step checklist used during the runtime 1.19 canary for TP (tensor-parallel) stability fixes.
- Primary goal: reduce/stop TP hangs + silent stalls without introducing unacceptable latency regressions.
- This doc is operational (who does what, what to watch, when to roll forward/back).

Owners / who to page
- Rollout driver (this checklist): Connor O’Brien (Eng Releases)
- Runtime TL: Noah Patel
- SRE on-point: Rafael Mendes
- Dashboards/alerts: Aisha Bello
- Dedicated PM/comms: Lauren Bishop + Paula Mendes
- Support escalation: Owen Phillips (for customer comms / ticket updates)

Scope of changes in this canary (runtime 1.19)
- Instrumentation
  - TP heartbeat metrics + stall reason codes (PR-21834)
  - NCCL counters + rank IDs in tracing spans (PR-21872)
- Correctness/stability fixes
  - Scheduler guardrail to prevent collective starvation (PR-21841)
  - NCCL stream/event synchronization hardening (PR-21853)
  - TP watchdog timeout + safe abort/replica drain (PR-21860)
  - KV cache compaction safety in TP (PR-21866)
  - Improve NCCL error surfacing to API layer (PR-21912)
- Reliability controls
  - Load-shed on TP stall signal (PR-21875)

Preflight (T-24h to T-1h)
1) Confirm build + deployment artifacts
- [ ] Runtime image tag / release candidate pinned and recorded in Linear ENG-4829
- [ ] Perf-canary build green for TP stress scenarios (perf-canary/pr-188)
- [ ] Observability pack dashboard panels merged/deployed (observability-pack/pr-412)
- [ ] Feature flags present in config management and can be toggled per cluster/account

2) Confirm dashboards + alert routing
- [ ] TP Stall + Timeout Dashboard is up-to-date (Confluence doc + Grafana link in ENG-4828)
- [ ] Alerts route correctly:
  - Dedicated canary cluster -> SRE oncall (page) + #eng-runtime (notify)
  - Hosted canary slice -> SRE oncall (page) + #eng-releases (notify)
- [ ] Alert dedupe/rate-limits enabled if applicable (see PR-21921 if already in the train; if not, set temporary alert silences for known noisy panels)

3) Baseline metrics snapshot (record in ENG-4829)
- Pull 7d baseline (or last stable window) for the target environment(s):
  - [ ] Request timeout rate (overall + TP-only)
  - [ ] p50/p95/p99 latency (prefill vs decode if available)
  - [ ] Replica drain/restart counts (and reasons)
  - [ ] NCCL error rate (hard errors) and “stall suspected” counters
  - [ ] TP heartbeat gap rate (per-rank) — should be near zero in healthy state
  - [ ] Scheduler queue depth / backpressure indicators
  - [ ] GPU utilization + SM occupancy (to catch “perf regression disguised as stability improvement”)

4) Canary target selection + comms readiness
- Dedicated-first rule for this rollout.
- [ ] Confirm Dedicated canary accounts (Lauren + Paula):
  - Acme AI (if opted-in and within the canary window)
  - 1–2 additional lower-risk Dedicated accounts / internal load tests
- [ ] Confirm Hosted canary slice definition (traffic %, regions) with SRE.
- [ ] Support prepared:
  - [ ] Owen has current workaround list + what info to collect (SUP doc)
  - [ ] Template update ready for affected tickets (SUP-48321/48344/48377)

Feature flags (expected names + defaults)
Note: actual config keys may differ by environment; confirm against deployment repo before go-live.
- tp_watchdog_enabled
  - Default: OFF initially in canary; turn ON after verifying instrumentation visibility.
- tp_watchdog_timeout_ms (or model-tiered thresholds)
  - Start conservative to avoid false positives; adjust only with runtime TL + SRE sign-off.
- tp_nccl_stream_sync_hardening
  - Default: ON in canary (but allow OFF for rollback if perf regression is too high).
- tp_scheduler_collective_starvation_guardrail
  - Default: ON in canary.
- tp_kv_compaction_safety
  - Default: ON in canary.
- tp_load_shed_on_stall
  - Default: ON in canary once stall detection is validated (prevents pile-ups).
- tp_extra_nccl_debug_logging
  - Default: OFF. Enable only during a defined window (ref: INT-2219) due to overhead + noise.

Go/no-go checklist (T-30m)
- [ ] SRE (Rafael) confirms no ongoing incidents / unrelated paging storm.
- [ ] Runtime TL (Noah) confirms RC includes intended PRs and no known blockers.
- [ ] Dashboard shows baseline health for last 60 minutes (no active stall clusters).
- [ ] All parties in the rollout channel (#eng-releases + #eng-sre bridge) and know the schedule.
- [ ] Rollback owner named for the window (usually Connor driving, Rafael executing infra rollback if needed).

Rollout steps — Dedicated canary
Step D1: Deploy runtime 1.19 RC to Dedicated canary cluster(s)
- [ ] Deploy with instrumentation + scheduler guardrail + NCCL hardening ON
- [ ] Keep watchdog OFF for first 30–60 minutes unless we are already in a degraded state
- [ ] Announce in #eng-releases + tag runtime + SRE + PM:
  - what changed, where, start time, and monitoring links

Step D2: Validate basic health (first 15 minutes)
- [ ] Error rate stable (no spike in 5xx / “engine abort” beyond expected)
- [ ] Latency within guardrails (see thresholds below)
- [ ] TP heartbeat present and updating for all ranks
- [ ] No abnormal increase in replica drains / crash loops

Step D3: Enable watchdog (guarded)
- [ ] Turn tp_watchdog_enabled ON for 1 canary shard / 1 cluster first
- [ ] Observe for 30 minutes:
  - Watchdog trigger count
  - Drain events attributable to watchdog
  - Customer-visible error codes (should be actionable, not generic timeouts)
  - Any evidence of “false positive” aborts during heavy prefill bursts
- [ ] If stable, expand watchdog ON to rest of Dedicated canary.

Step D4: Optional: enable extra NCCL debug logging (only if needed)
- Preconditions:
  - [ ] There is an active suspected NCCL-ordering issue OR unclear stall signature
  - [ ] Approved in INT-2219 (or equivalent) with a start/end time
- [ ] Enable for max 30–60 minutes.
- [ ] Confirm log volume acceptable + no customer data leakage concerns.
- [ ] Disable and verify logs revert.

Rollout steps — Hosted canary
Only proceed after Dedicated canary is stable for a minimum window.
- Suggested minimum windows:
  - 4 hours stable for “normal” weekday traffic
  - Overnight window if risk appetite is low

Step H1: Deploy to Hosted canary slice
- [ ] Start with smallest slice (e.g., 1–5% traffic) and one region first if possible
- [ ] Keep watchdog ON only if Dedicated showed low false positives
- [ ] Ensure routing/fallback behavior is correct for surfaced error codes (PR-21912)

Step H2: Ramp
- [ ] Increase slice in planned steps (e.g., 5% -> 25% -> 50% -> 100%) only after meeting success criteria.

Monitoring & success criteria (during canary)
Primary stability metrics
- Hang/stall proxies:
  - TP heartbeat gaps: should trend down vs baseline, and should not show multi-minute gaps for any rank without corresponding drain/abort
  - Request timeouts: should decrease vs baseline in TP-heavy routes
  - “In-flight collective counter stuck” / stall reason counts: should be rare and correlated to safe abort, not indefinite hang

Secondary metrics (guardrails)
- p99 latency: must not regress >10% for the primary canary workload class (prefill/decode tracked separately if possible)
- Throughput: no sustained drop >5% at steady load (watch for NCCL sync overhead)
- Replica churn: drain/restart should not exceed baseline by >2x for >30 minutes
- Error budget: new error codes from abort path should be < agreed threshold (set with PM + SRE; typically <0.1% of requests)

Rollback triggers (stop-the-line)
Immediate rollback (no debate; page runtime TL + SRE lead)
- [ ] Hard NCCL errors spike (any sustained increase indicating systemic comms failure)
- [ ] Widespread watchdog-triggered drains across replicas (suggesting false positive threshold too low or systemic perf regression)
- [ ] p99 latency regression >20% sustained for 15+ minutes with customer impact
- [ ] New deadlock/hang signature appears (no drain, no abort, heartbeat stalls across ranks)

Conditional rollback / hold ramp (investigate first)
- [ ] Moderate p99 regression (10–20%) without timeouts improvement
- [ ] Watchdog triggers present but correlate to real stuck collectives (i.e., improving timeouts) — may be acceptable temporarily
- [ ] Increased load-shed/rejections (may be intended protective behavior; confirm with PM)

Rollback procedure (quick)
1) If perf regression suspected but stability improved
- [ ] First try disabling tp_nccl_stream_sync_hardening (if feature-flagged safely) while leaving instrumentation on
- [ ] Keep scheduler guardrail on (low risk) unless proven to regress significantly

2) If watchdog false positives suspected
- [ ] Disable tp_watchdog_enabled
- [ ] Keep stall detection metrics on so we can still see heartbeat gaps
- [ ] Revert timeout value only if there is a known-good previous value

3) If systemic instability / new hang
- [ ] Roll back runtime to previous stable version for the canary cluster/slice
- [ ] Drain/replace affected replicas
- [ ] Announce rollback + current state in the rollout channel and update ENG-4829

Customer comms checklist (Dedicated)
- Owner: Lauren + Paula (with Support/CS)
- Before enabling on an enterprise Dedicated account:
  - [ ] Confirm opt-in + maintenance window expectations
  - [ ] Confirm which mitigations are currently active (concurrency caps, batch limits, disabled kernel paths)
- During the canary:
  - [ ] Provide status update if there is a visible change (either improvement or increased abort errors)
  - [ ] If watchdog triggers cause customer-visible errors, communicate that this is protective behavior preventing long hangs/timeouts
- After canary success:
  - [ ] Provide “what changed” summary + next ramp schedule
  - [ ] Ask for confirmation on observed timeout rate improvements on their side

Support ticket hygiene
- [ ] Update SUP-48321 / SUP-48344 / SUP-48377 with:
  - runtime version
  - whether watchdog enabled
  - current mitigations still required (if any)
  - what logs/metrics we are collecting
- [ ] If customer sees new errors: capture request IDs + error codes (post-PR-21912 should be more actionable)

Data to capture during the window (for post-rollout review)
- [ ] Before/after snapshot of the baseline metrics list (timeouts, p99, drains, heartbeat gaps)
- [ ] Top stall reasons by count (if available)
- [ ] Any clusters/accounts where metrics diverged from the mean (outliers)
- [ ] Notes about any manual interventions (drains, flag flips, log enablement)

Post-canary exit criteria
- [ ] Dedicated canary shows statistically meaningful reduction in timeouts/hang proxies across at least one peak period
- [ ] No Sev1/Sev2 triggered by the change
- [ ] Guardrails met (latency/throughput acceptable)
- [ ] Runbook updated if we learned new operational steps (Confluence runtime-tp-hang-mitigation)
- [ ] ENG-4829 updated with final go/no-go decision + next rollout step

Scratch / open questions (keep updated during rollout)
- What’s the current recommended default watchdog timeout by model tier? (link to #eng-runtime/1749973309 thread)
- Do we want watchdog ON by default in Hosted after Dedicated success, or keep it opt-in for one more release?
- Any evidence that NCCL sync hardening affects CUDA graph capture performance for specific models/hardware?

Last updated
- 2025-03-03: Added explicit rollback order (disable NCCL sync vs disable watchdog) + clarified Dedicated-first minimum stability window before Hosted.
